To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rapid thermal annealing at high temperatures (up to 700 ° C ) of MBE-grown layers of GaBixAs _{1-x} with x = 6% leads to the reduction of the photoexcited carriers lifetime by two orders of the magnitude.
the annealing process has a dual effect: it leads to an enhancement of the radiative recombination rate, but at the same time it increases the nonradiative recombination rate.
the carrier dynamics of GaBiAs layers is strongly influenced by thermal annealing, especially in the layers with high Bi content.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of rapid thermal annealing on the photoexcited carrier decay in GaBiAs layers.
the effect of rapid thermal annealing on photoexcited carriers dynamics in MBE grown GaBixAs(1-x) layers.
the effect of thermal annealing on the photoexcited carrier lifetime in GaBiAs layers with a low and high Bi composition, grown by MBE on GaAs (001) substrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thermal annealing of GaBiAs layers has a dual effect.
the annealing process has no significant effect on the electron lifetime in the GaBi0xAs1−x layer.
the thermal annealing has a strong impact on the carrier dynamics of GaBiAs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Bi content in GaBiAs has a strong influence on carrier dynamics.
the Bi composition in GaBiAs is the main factor that influences the electron recombination process.
the Bi content in the GaBiAs alloy is an important factor for the recombination process and the Bi composition should be carefully controlled to achieve a long carrier lifetime.

the annealing of the GaBiAs layer at temperatures up to about 600 °C can be used as an effective method for the optimization of the carrier dynamics in this material.
the annealing effect is a promising tool for the control of photoexcited carrier recombination dynamics in GaBiAs.
